body:
Did you change the "Save Scene As..." shortcut to something else, they might conflict here

Also is the script editor open? It takes precedence and might catch the shortcut as well

yes it seems as it is interferring here a bit.

Let me express this with different words (sorry english is not my first language):

"In most applications there is _one_ and only _one_ `Save all` setting to save... well... _all_ changed files, no matter which type they have"

I see absolutely no sense in different shortcuts for saving scripts, scenes, shaders and I don't know what else. Just save all open changes! If a tab has a (*) in it, save it. that's what I want/expect from a "save all" function. not more, not less.

if, for some reason, it is necessary anywhere to have different shortcuts, at least it should be possible to assign all those different "save alls" the same shortcut, so a user could "tweak" this to the own needs.

That is not really relevant to this issue though, that's more of a [proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals)

So let's focus on the issue here of it failing to register

So:
* Have you changed the "Save Scene As..." shortcut so you don't have conflicting shortcuts?
* Does it work when the script editor is not focused?

If it works with both of those this is not a bug but how the editor focus system works, to allow having shortcuts more manageably as there are only so many shortcuts available, and you don't get confusing behavior affecting the script editor without it being focused, though it also causes other confusion when shortcuts fail to work if you don't know it requires focus, etc.

My apologies, you are right. So, taking a look at the _default_ settings, they seem to be already conflicting out-of-the-box? (shader & script). But I must say I am not 100% sure from all my experiments, whether this is really the default, what we see here (no "undo-arrow" icons in the key bindings so I can't say which are default) I tried to set them all apart and alone this sheer number of required "x..S" combinations tells us, there's something conceptionally wrong going on. So i tried with Alt+S to save shaders as I almost ran out of usefuls alt/shift/ctrl combinations. Now we have all possible combinations in place, if i see it right (Shift+S can not be used as its just the upper case S character) so now we have * i changed a script and hit Ctrl+S (Save Scene) but the script got saved. * then i changed a scene and hit Alt+S but this shortcut seems to open the "Shader Editor" Tab on bottom (another conflict? why does this one work?) * Ctrl-S also saves the scene (so ctrl+S reacts on both, scene and script, event when script is set to something else). * Alt+Ctrl+S saved the script (same as Ctrl+S but this should save the "scene") So, in case you save the script, because it part of a "scene" (i.e. attached to some player or monster object), this would even increase confusion, if we also had to differ between "scripts as part of a scene" and "scripts that are standalone", if such even exist as everything is somehow connected to some kind of node). The "solution" to this behavior (not sure whether it's correct to call it a "bug") is: simplify that and take out all that unnecessary complexity. It's just saving. It's a common standard to have Ctrl-S save the current file and (in most apps) Shift+Ctrl+S to "Save all". If you prefer, I will happily open a feature request - I am new to the engine, so bare with me from my first ticket. See it as input of a confused first time user. 😄 Please don't get me wrong, I love the engine so far, it looks great and it feels great, but customizing the save system (or: _simplifying_ it) looks like a boss-quest to me. This is really unintuitive and waaaay over-engineered imho.

I'd say that the different contexts are by design, you don't want to save a scene accidentally when you're working on a script, and vice versa

`Alt+S` is the shortcut for opening the shader dock, so that works as expected, but it shouldn't be relevant here as you didn't bind anything to it for saving 

The interface might take some time to get used to, but it's very flexible and useful when you know how it works and allows you to have control over what specifically you want to do, but as with all IDEs you need to consider conflicting shortcuts 

But if you feel this can be improved on please do open a proposal (after checking for open ones)

But I don't see anything not working as it's designed to here from what I can tell, save for `Ctrl + S` saving the script, not sure about that one, will see if I can replicate

Thanks for taking the time to answer with this detail!

As far as I can see, I have only the choice between 
- "remember all those shortcuts" 
- "click menu->save" 
- or run the game... for this, a "save all" seems to be possible with no troubles 😉-- so why can't we have exactly this as one shortcut?? <-- this is, what my proposal will be

And also thanks for trying to replicate! If you can't, you may close this issue.

Cheers, Gris
